test_title: PYST 05: RRB Group D Official Paper GS - (Held On: 28 Nov, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question:
Which of the following statements is/are correct?

a. Olfactory indicators are used to check the acidic or basic nature of a compound.

b. Clove oil is an olfactory indicator.

c. Clove oil is used to check the purity of any compound.
solution:
The correct answer is __**a and b only**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Olfactory indicators** are substances whose smell changes when exposed to acidic or basic environments. This characteristic makes them useful in determining whether a solution is acidic or basic. ***Hence, statement a is correct.***
 
• **Clove oil** is one of the examples of olfactory indicators. Its smell changes depending on whether it is in an acidic or basic medium. ***Hence, statement b is correct.***
 
• **Clove oil** is not used to test the purity of compounds. Its primary role is as an olfactory indicator for identifying the nature of solutions (acidic or basic), not for purity testing. ***Hence, statement c is incorrect.***
 
• ***Therefore, the correct answer is a and b only.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Olfactory Indicators:**

 
 
• Olfactory indicators are substances that exhibit a change in smell when exposed to acidic or basic solutions.
 
• These indicators are particularly useful in laboratories where their unique smell can help identify the nature of a compound.
 
• Examples of olfactory indicators include clove oil, vanilla essence, and onion extract.
 
• They are primarily utilized in qualitative analysis to identify acids and bases.
 
 
 
• **Clove Oil:**
 
 
• Clove oil is extracted from the clove plant and contains **eugenol**, which gives it its characteristic smell.
 
• It is a widely recognized olfactory indicator due to the noticeable change in smell when exposed to acidic or basic environments.
 
• Clove oil has applications in aromatherapy and as a flavoring agent besides its use as an olfactory indicator.
 
• It is not employed for checking the purity of compounds; rather, it is used for identifying the acidic or basic nature of solutions.
 
 
 
• **Other Types of Indicators:**
 
 
• **Natural Indicators:** Substances like turmeric, litmus, and red cabbage extract are used to distinguish between acidic and basic solutions based on color change.
 
• **Synthetic Indicators:** Examples include phenolphthalein and methyl orange, which exhibit distinct color changes in acidic or basic solutions.
 
• **Universal Indicators:** These are mixtures of indicators that provide a range of colors for different pH levels, giving a more precise measurement of acidity or alkalinity.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Applications of Indicators:**

 
 
• Indicators are essential in titration experiments to determine the endpoint of a reaction.
 
• They help identify the pH of solutions in various scientific and industrial processes.
 
• Olfactory indicators are specifically useful in environments where visual indicators may not be practical.
 
 
 
• **Limitations:**
 
 
• Olfactory indicators may not work effectively if the smell of the solution itself is overpowering.
 
• These indicators are qualitative and may not provide precise measurements of pH.
